study.name: phoenix-flat-bsm
study.source_text:
# Phoenix under flat Black-Scholes.
#
# The same three arms as the snowball study -- two-surface PDE, quadrature, and
# one paired-RQMC benchmark -- over a payoff with one extra hard feature: a
# coupon barrier. A phoenix pays a coupon at every observation where spot sits
# above 85, knock-out or not, so every observation date carries a digital. That
# is where a deterministic grid and Monte Carlo tend to part company first,
# which is why near_coupon parks spot right on the barrier.
#
# Economic scale, environment and bounds are identical to snowball_flat_bsm, on
# purpose: with multiplier 200, inception spot 100 and notional 20,000 the delta
# quantum and the reference move are both exactly 1.0, so a raw error IS a
# contract error -- and the two certifications sit on the same axis.
#
# Bound calibration (release procedure section 7, step 4). The cell gate needs
# the benchmark standard error inside 0.25 x 0.5 = 0.125 c. Measured at this
# sampling budget (4 batches x 65,536 paths, paired bumps): pv 0.0033, delta
# 0.0035, gamma 0.0052 -- a 24-38x margin. Desk tolerance and benchmark
# resolution are compatible, so the bound is not one the sampling cannot cash.
#
# Offline study (minutes, not seconds). Run it with:
#   python -m quantark.modelvalidation run example/modelvalidation/phoenix_flat_bsm.yaml
# Add --quick for a wiring check that is explicitly not bankable evidence.

study: phoenix-flat-bsm
schema: 1

quantities: [pv, delta, gamma]

bounds:
  cell: 0.5
  mean_signed_bias: 0.1

sampling:
  paths_per_batch: 65536
  min_batches: 4
  max_batches: 32
  seed: 20260818
  bump: 0.01

economic_scale:
  builder: hedge_contracts
  params:
    hedge_multiplier: 200.0
    hedge_inception_spot: 100.0
    notional: 20000.0

environment:
  builder: flat_bsm
  params:
    spot: 100.0
    vol: 0.22
    rate: 0.025
    div_yield: 0.03

product:
  builder: equity.phoenix
  params:
    initial_price: 100.0
    strike: 100.0
    ko_barrier: 103.0
    ko_rate: 0.0
    ki_barrier: 75.0
    coupon_barrier: 85.0
    coupon_rate: 0.02
    num_observations: 12
    memory_coupon: false
    maturity: 1.0
    contract_multiplier: 1.0

reference:
  builder: equity.phoenix.mc_rqmc
  params: {}

candidates:
  - builder: equity.phoenix.pde
    params: {accuracy: standard}
  - builder: equity.phoenix.quad
    params: {grid_points: 1001}

cases:
  # At inception, clear of all three barriers.
  - {name: ordinary}
  # Just under the knock-out barrier: the KO discontinuity sits inside the bump
  # stencil, which is where deterministic gamma usually breaks first.
  - {name: near_ko, environment: {spot: 102.5}}
  # Sitting ON the coupon barrier. A phoenix coupon is a digital at 85, so its
  # sensitivity is maximal here and the whole coupon stream is in play.
  - {name: near_coupon, environment: {spot: 85.5}}
  # Just above the knock-in barrier: the terminal payoff turns over here.
  - {name: near_ki, environment: {spot: 76.0}}
  # Low vol: barriers are rarely reached, so the grid resolves a much narrower
  # region of interest and the coupon stream is nearly certain.
  - {name: low_vol, environment: {vol: 0.12}}
  # Three months with a quarterly schedule: few observations left, and time
  # discretization error has nowhere to average out.
  - {name: near_expiry, product: {num_observations: 3, maturity: 0.25}}
  # Memory coupons: missed coupons accumulate and pay later. A prior audit found
  # the PDE paying accrued memory coupons at KO regardless of the coupon-barrier
  # condition, so this path carries history and must be certified explicitly.
  - {name: memory, product: {memory_coupon: true}}
  # Step-down barriers: KO and coupon barriers both decline 0.5% of initial
  # price per observation. Twenty-four distinct levels now compete for grid
  # alignment where every case above had two, and the coupon digital moves to a
  # new strike at every observation instead of sitting still.
  - {name: stepdown, product: {ko_stepdown: 0.005, coupon_stepdown: 0.005}}
  # Discretely monitored KI. Unreachable until 2026-08-19: PhoenixOption built
  # only its KO observation schedule, so a discrete KI phoenix raised rather
  # than priced, and no certified cell used anything but continuous KI.
  - {name: discrete_ki, product: {ki_monitoring: discrete}}
  # A KI barrier declining 0.5% of initial price per observation, 75 -> 69.5.
  - {name: ki_stepdown, product: {ki_monitoring: discrete, ki_stepdown: 0.005}}
  # Once knocked in the KO stops applying, so the knocked-in surface carries the
  # coupon stream on to maturity unbarriered.
  - {name: disable_ko_after_ki, product: {disable_ko_after_ki: true}}
  # Reverse phoenix: call payoff, DOWN knock-out, UP knock-in and coupon
  # barriers. Every barrier mask in the vector-surface solver inverts.
  - {name: reverse, product: {is_reverse: true, ko_barrier: 97.0, ki_barrier: 125.0,
                              coupon_barrier: 115.0}}
  # Coupons rolled up and paid when the note ENDS -- at the knock-out settlement
  # if it knocks out, at maturity otherwise. The payment date is path-dependent,
  # so a fixed discount cannot express it: the deterministic engines carry a
  # termination-value surface and the benchmark pays the roll-up at knock-out.
  - {name: coupon_at_expiry, product: {coupon_pay_type: expiry}}
  # The roll-up meeting the memory ladder: accrued coupons are released on a
  # later coupon date and then still wait for termination to be paid.
  - {name: coupon_at_expiry_memory, product: {coupon_pay_type: expiry,
                                              memory_coupon: true}}
